title: Rhubarb and orange compote with yoghurt

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Rhubarb, orange, honey, almonds, pumpkin seeds, Greek yoghurt and ground ginger are all plain home-kitchen foods.

supermarket.reason: Forced rhubarb is stocked by mainstream supermarkets in January, and everything else is an everyday item.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a small lidded pan and a frying pan, and simmering and dry-toasting are beginner techniques.

works.reason: 400g rhubarb with an orange and 2 tbsp honey, simmered covered for 6 to 8 minutes, gives a tart but pleasant compote over 125g yoghurt each, with enough nuts for four.

honest_times.reason: Cutting rhubarb, zesting and juicing an orange and chopping almonds fits in 10 minutes, and the 10 minutes of cooking matches the simmer and toasting.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the ginger are used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm compote of forced rhubarb suits a January morning, and the rhubarb is clearly the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English, like a cook explaining to a neighbour.

hearty_healthy.reason: Yoghurt, fruit, nuts and seeds make a real, filling breakfast with modest added sugar.
